My goal is to maximize my utility, given my values for each school (w=$60, x=$73, y=$57, z=$55) and my priority rank at each school (w:1, x:2, y:1, z:2). I also know that most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

My true preferences are x > w > y > z.

Let's analyze some scenarios:

Scenario 1: Everyone else ranks y > x > w > z.
- If I rank truthfully (x > w > y > z), I will likely get w, since x and y will be highly contested.
- If I rank x > y > w > z, I might get x if my priority is high enough.
- If I rank y > x > w > z, I might get y if my priority is high enough.
- If I rank w > x > y > z, I might get w.

Scenario 2: Some people rank x higher than y.
- My chances of getting x increase.

Since I have a high priority at w and y, I should consider ranking one of them first. However, x is my most preferred school, and I have a decent priority there (2).

Consider ranking x first. If I don't get x, I want to have a good backup. Since I have priority 1 at w and y, I want to rank one of them second. Since w > y, I should rank w second.

Therefore, my ranking should be x > w > y > z. This gives me the best chance of getting my top choice (x), and a good backup (w) if I don't get x. Ranking y before w would be suboptimal, as I value w more than y.

Finally, I rank w last, since it has the lowest value.

Therefore, my ranking should be x > y > z > w.
